chunks: I got married in Medina, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'How do you find her?' I said, 'Whatever good a man may find in a woman, I have found it in her — but she betrayed me.' So he said: 'And what is it?' I said, 'She gave birth to a girl.'
Verily, Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: 'your parents and your children — you know not which of them is nearer to you in benefit.'

key_terms.جارية: Girl, young female; also used for a female slave; here meaning a newborn daughter
key_terms.خانتني: She betrayed/failed me; the narrator's use of this word reveals his disappointment at having a daughter rather than a son
key_terms.عزَّ وجلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — a common honorific for God (Allah 'azza wa jalla)
key_terms.نفعاً: Benefit, usefulness; the Quran emphasizes that we cannot know which of our relatives will benefit us most

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about having daughters in Islam?
ai.summary: A man complains to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) that his wife 'betrayed' him by giving birth to a daughter, implying he had hoped for a son. The Imam gently corrects this attitude, quoting Quran 4:11 to remind him that God alone knows which child or parent will bring greater benefit — daughters should not be devalued. This hadith reflects the Imam's pedagogical approach of using Quranic verses to correct cultural biases against daughters inherited from pre-Islamic Arab custom.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, Bin Bazie, from Ibrahim Bin Mihzam, from Ibrahim Al Karkhy, from a reliable one from his companions who narrated to him, said, 
‘I got married at Al-Medina, so Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘How do you view?’ I said, ‘Whatever a man views from the goodness regarding a wife except that I have seen it in her, but she betrayed me’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And what is it?’ I said, ‘She gave birth to a girl’.
Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [4:11] your parents and your children, you know not which of them is the nearer to you in benefit’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il ibn Bazi‘ from Ibrahim ibn Mehzam from Ibrahim al-Karkhiy from a trustworthy man who narrated from certain persons of our people who have said the following: “I married in al-Madinah and abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, asked me, ‘How is your married life?’ I replied, ‘Every good thing that a man can see in a woman I found with her but she betrayed me.’ He (the Imam) asked, ‘How did she do so?’ I replied, ‘She gave birth to a girl.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘You may have disliked her

but Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, says, ‘Regardless of how you feel about your parents or children, you do not know which of them is more beneficial to you. Allah is All-knowing and All-wise. [4:11]’”
